name: Anti-Slop Rulebook
summary: Patterns that make a website look AI-generated. Everything here is a don't; the positive counterparts live in the other rulebooks.
check: Run `node scripts/proui-scan.mjs <src>` and review every finding in context.
Compare screenshots at 390 and 1440 px against this list, section by section.
Search the build for counting labels (`01`, `/ 05`, `No.`) and placeholder text.

rules.title: Purple-to-blue gradients
rules.text: The default "AI startup" gradient. Pick colours that come from the brand, the product or its photography instead.

rules.title: Gradient backgrounds as filler
rules.text: A gradient behind a section in place of real content or imagery. Acceptable as one signature brand element; slop when every section has one.

rules.title: Glowing background orbs
rules.text: Blurred coloured blobs floating behind content to add "depth".

rules.title: Glassmorphism everywhere
rules.text: Frosted translucent panels on every card. Use only where something really sits above imagery (a header over a photo, a sheet over a map).

rules.title: Pointless shadows
rules.text: Strong drop shadows on everything. Use elevation only to show that something floats (menus, dialogs, dragged items).

rules.title: Low-contrast dark mode
rules.text: Grey text on near-black that is hard to read. See `DC-15`.

rules.title: Too many shades and opacities
rules.text: Text at 70 %, 50 %, 40 % and 30 %, five greys, three tints of one colour. Use a small, named palette: typically ink, muted, surface, border, one accent, one danger.

rules.title: Dithering and grain as decoration
rules.text: Pixel-dither or noise effects on images and gradients because they are trendy.

rules.title: Three feature cards in a row
rules.text: Icon, title and two lines, three times. Show the feature itself (screenshot, demo, numbers) or use a layout that fits the content.

rules.title: Empty bento grids
rules.text: A grid of uneven tiles holding an icon and four words each. Bento only works when each tile holds something real to look at.

rules.title: Generic three-tier pricing
rules.text: Starter, Pro and Enterprise with "Most popular" in the middle, even when the product has one price. Show the pricing the business actually has.

rules.title: Containers with borders
rules.text: Every block wrapped in a bordered box, boxes inside boxes. Separate content with spacing first (`DC-08`), borders second.

rules.title: Overusing dividers
rules.text: Hairlines between everything. Whitespace usually does the job.

rules.title: Tags and pills everywhere
rules.text: Small rounded labels on every item without a job to do.

rules.title: Badges above headlines
rules.text: "New", "Introducing" or a sparkle chip above every heading. Use one only for real news.

rules.title: Eyebrows on every heading
rules.text: A small kicker above each title ("FEATURES" above "Our features"). Fine occasionally when it adds information (a date or a category), never a number.

rules.title: Decorative counting
rules.text: No counting labels anywhere: no "01 / 02 / 03" on sections, no "001", "(02)", "No. 3" or "04 —" on cards, photos, features, services, FAQ items, steps, slides or list rows, no "1/5" image counters, no numbered form steps ("1 Contact", "2 Delivery"). Give each item a name instead ("Contact", "Delivery"), and let order come from position. This holds even when the order is real and even inside styles that otherwise like catalogues or grids. Numbers that are data stay: prices, sizes, dates, times, quantities, stock left, order IDs, measurements.

rules.title: Squircles everywhere
rules.text: iOS-style super-rounded squares on every icon and card.

rules.title: Untouched component library
rules.text: shadcn/ui (or any kit) in its default look. Restyle it to the brand: colours, radii, type, spacing, states.

rules.title: Over-the-top detailed UI mockups
rules.text: Fake dashboards crowded with tiny charts and numbers that show nothing real. Show the actual product (`DC-06`).

rules.title: Overly detailed diagrams
rules.text: Complex schematics that look clever and explain nothing.

rules.title: Instrument Serif and the default "AI serif" look
rules.text: Instrument Serif (often italic) mixed into headlines has become a cliché. Choose type for the brand.

rules.title: Excessive italics
rules.text: Random single words in italics for "elegance". Italics need a reason.

rules.title: Negative kerning on body text
rules.text: Tight tracking is fine on large display headlines and nowhere else.

rules.title: Excessive mono fonts
rules.text: Monospace on every label to look "technical". Use mono for data that benefits from it: prices, timers, codes, IDs, specs. See `DC-04`.

rules.title: ALL CAPS subtitles everywhere
rules.text: Wide-tracked uppercase on every label and subheading.

rules.title: Periods in titles
rules.text: "Built for speed." on every heading. Fine as an occasional voice choice, slop as a rule.

rules.title: Gradient-filled headline text
rules.text: Headlines filled with a colour gradient.

rules.title: Lucide icons everywhere
rules.text: The default icon set on every line. Use icons only where they help scanning, from one consistent set (`DC-12`), styled to the brand.

rules.title: Emojis in headings and UI
rules.text: "🚀 Fast", "🔒 Secure". Never in headings, buttons or navigation.

rules.title: Sparkle icons for anything "AI" or "new"
rules.text: ✨ as decoration.

rules.title: Code breadcrumbs as decoration
rules.text: `~/app`, `// comments`, `{ }` and terminal chrome on a site that is not about code.

rules.title: ASCII art and ASCII animations
rules.text: Text-character imagery used as an effect.

rules.title: Cursor-following beams and spotlights
rules.text: Glows that chase the pointer. Effect for its own sake.

rules.title: Everything fades in on scroll
rules.text: Every block sliding and fading as it enters. It slows reading and tires people. Animate a few key moments only (section 4).

rules.title: Bouncy everyday UI
rules.text: Springy overshoot on menus, toggles and dialogs (`MO-13`).

rules.title: Em dashes everywhere
rules.text: A dash in every sentence is the clearest sign of generated copy. Use commas, full stops and colons.

rules.title: "It's not X, it's Y" phrasing
rules.text: "It's not just a tool, it's a revolution." Say what it does.

rules.title: Generic hero copy
rules.text: "Supercharge your workflow", "The future of X". Write a specific headline (`DC-09`).

rules.title: Verbose, redundant text
rules.text: Paragraphs that repeat the heading in other words. Cut it in half.

rules.title: Vague button labels
rules.text: "Get started", "Learn more", "Submit". Say what happens: "Download the price list", "Book a 20-minute call", "Place order".

rules.title: Claims without proof
rules.text: "10× faster", "Trusted by thousands" without numbers, sources or names. Back it up or remove it.

rules.title: Fake testimonials
rules.text: Invented quotes from "Sarah K., CEO" with stock headshots. Use real ones or none. Never present invented reviews as genuine.

rules.title: Placeholder business info
rules.text: Lorem ipsum, "123 Main Street", info@company.com, fake phone numbers left in the build.

rules.title: No real product demo
rules.text: Abstract illustrations instead of screenshots, video or a live demo.

rules.title: Broken third-party embeds
rules.text: Maps, videos, calendars or chat widgets that fail to load or break the layout. Test every embed and give it a fallback.

rules.title: Forms asking for too much
rules.text: Phone, company, job title and budget before any value is shown. Ask only what is needed now.

rules.title: Keyboard-unfriendly forms
rules.text: Wrong tab order, Enter does not submit, no visible focus. See `ST-09`.

rules.title: Side-stripe accent borders
rules.text: A thick coloured `border-left` (or right) on cards, callouts, list items or alerts as decoration. Use a full border, a tinted background, an icon or nothing.

rules.title: Accent border on a rounded card
rules.text: A one-side coloured border bent around a large radius. It reads as a template and the corner looks broken.

rules.title: Nested cards
rules.text: A card inside a card inside a card. Flatten: one surface, grouping by spacing (`DC-08`, `LY-05`).

rules.title: Hard offset shadows by reflex
rules.text: The solid black `4px 4px 0` "neo-brutalist" shadow on every button and card. Keep it only when a chosen style (`PLAYFUL POP`, `POSTER COLLAGE`) asks for it, and then use it consistently.

rules.title: Thin border plus wide soft shadow
rules.text: A 1 px grey border and a huge blurred shadow on the same card. Pick one way to show elevation.

rules.title: Dark glow
rules.text: Coloured `box-shadow` or `drop-shadow` glows on dark backgrounds (neon edges, glowing buttons). Light is not a decoration.

rules.title: Radial halo or spotlight behind the hero
rules.text: A soft radial gradient centred behind the headline to "add depth". Related to `SL-03`.

rules.title: Grid and stripe backgrounds
rules.text: Faint graph-paper lines, dot grids or repeating diagonal stripes behind sections to look technical. Allowed when the grid is real content (a plan, a chart, a cutting mat for a craft shop) or a chosen style asks for it, used once.

rules.title: Icon tile stack
rules.text: A rounded square tile with an icon, then a title, then two lines, repeated. The most common generated component. Show the thing itself.

rules.title: Hero eyebrow chip
rules.text: A pill above the hero headline ("✦ Now with AI", "v2.0 is here"). Covered by `SL-15`; listed so audits can name it.

rules.title: Overused display faces
rules.text: Inter, Roboto, Geist, Space Grotesk, Plus Jakarta Sans, DM Sans, Outfit, Instrument Sans, Syne, Fraunces, Playfair Display, Cormorant, Newsreader and Instrument Serif as the *display* face by default. They are fine for UI text in an app (`TY-02`); as a headline face they say "I stopped looking". Choosing one needs a reason no other face satisfies.

rules.title: Flat type hierarchy
rules.text: Heading sizes less than about 1.25× apart, so nothing leads (`TY-05`).

rules.title: Oversized H1 by reflex
rules.text: A giant headline that pushes the action below the fold and wraps into a stack of one-word lines. Big type is a choice of a style (`MEGA TYPE`), not a default.

rules.title: Extreme negative tracking
rules.text: Letter-spacing tighter than about `-0.04em` on any text, or any negative tracking below about 32 px.

rules.title: Italic serif display by reflex
rules.text: One italic serif word in a sans headline ("Design that *feels*"). Related to `SL-22`, `SL-23`.

rules.title: Cream, terracotta and serif
rules.text: Warm off-white ground, high-contrast serif headline and a terracotta or signal-red accent, used because the subject is "warm", "bookish" or "human". It is one of the four looks generated sites fall into.

rules.title: Near-black and one neon
rules.text: Black ground, one acid or neon accent, glowing edges. The second default look.

rules.title: Broadsheet costume
rules.text: Hairline rules, italic display serif and tiny tracked mono labels on a site that is not a publication. The third default look.

rules.title: Neo-brutalist kit
rules.text: Flat saturated ink, black boxes, hard offset shadows and heavy condensed type, used by default. The fourth default look. All four (`SL-64` to `SL-67`) are fine when the brief or a style keyword asks for them; landing in one without being asked means the direction was not chosen.

rules.title: Marquee filler
rules.text: An endless scrolling ticker of logos or adjectives because the page felt empty. A marquee needs real content (real client logos, real news) and must pause for reduced motion.

rules.title: Pulsing dots and blinking cursors
rules.text: "Live" dots and typing cursors as decoration on content that is not live.

rules.title: Shape-assembled illustrations
rules.text: Pictures built from CSS circles and rectangles, or many-point `clip-path` polygons and blob masks where a real image, icon or drawing belongs.

rules.title: Aphoristic cadence
rules.text: Short punchy fragments in threes ("Fast. Simple. Yours."), slogans in place of information, and buzzwords ("seamless", "unlock", "elevate", "empower", "next-level", "game-changing"). See `CP-03`.

rules.title: Content hidden at rest
rules.text: Text or images that stay invisible until a scroll animation fires, so the page is blank without JavaScript, in screenshots, for crawlers, or when the animation fails. Content is visible by default; motion only enhances it (`MO`, `PF-21`).

rules.title: Icons and pictures on content cards
rules.text: A small icon, emoji or clip-art picture on top of every service, feature, standard or value card. On professional sites (property, finance, law, architecture, luxury) it reads as a template and cheapens the content. Let the title and the copy lead, or show the real thing (a photo of the work, a number, a screenshot). Icons belong in controls, dense data and navigation aids; decorative card icons are acceptable on social media graphics and playful consumer brands (`SL-29`, `SL-57`).
